This executable example loads the certified Poincaré homology-sphere fixture,
plots its feasible α-cut layout, and computes the fixed production plot.
Julia owns the geometry; the website displays the very same SVG, without
browser-only deformation. No tuning sliders are required.

The mathematical code comes from Klebanov Fig. 2.15; its region decoration is
a reconstruction candidate, not a directly transcribed source datum. The seed
below is a saved fixture-scoped feasible layout, not evidence of a complete
general-purpose router.

```{julia}
using Topology

const H = Topology.Heegaard
const ROOT = dirname(Base.active_project())

diagram_path = joinpath(ROOT, "test", "fixtures",
                        "poincare_homology_sphere_v1.hgd.json")
layout_path = joinpath(ROOT, "test", "fixtures",
                       "poincare_homology_sphere_v1.hgd.layout.json")

diagram = H.certify_heegaard(H.load_heegaard(diagram_path))
feasible = H.load_layout(layout_path, diagram)
```

## Before — certified feasible layout

```{julia}
H.plot(feasible)
```

## After — fixed production plot

```{julia}
figure = H.plot(diagram, feasible)
figure
```

## Verification and provenance

```{julia}
smoothing = figure.backend_trace["smoothing"]
plot_trace = figure.backend_trace["plot"]

(
    valid = figure.report.valid,
    crossings = length(figure.crossings),
    diagram_hash = figure.diagram_hash,
    profile = plot_trace["profile"],
    slider_values = plot_trace["review_slider_values"],
    measured_minimum = smoothing["minimum_flattened_separation"],
    stop_reason = smoothing["stop_reason"],
    converged = smoothing["converged"],
)
```

## Persist the plotted result

```{julia}
output_dir = joinpath(ROOT, "artifacts", "heegaard", "qmd_plot")
mkpath(output_dir)

svg_path = joinpath(output_dir, "poincare-alpha-cut.svg")
layout_output_path = joinpath(output_dir,
                              "poincare-alpha-cut.hgd.layout.json")

H.render(figure; backend=:svg, path=svg_path)
H.save_layout(layout_output_path, figure)

(svg = svg_path, layout = layout_output_path)
```

The reported minimum distance is measured on adaptively flattened curves.
An iteration limit or stalled line search is not a proof of optimality.
